sentences.text: Hi there listeners and welcome to today’s edition of The Classical.
I'm your host David Choi and today’s program focuses on board gaming.
I have two people with me in the studio today to help discuss this and they are firstly Angel Fu.
Hello David. who is a local board game producer, that’s right isn’t it?
That's right David.
And also Eric Park, who is a well -known board game designer from California California in the USA.
Hi David, glad to be in Hong Kong.
So, Angel. I understand that you've started your own local board game company.
That's right. And what's the name of your company?
Griffin Workshop. So why did you decide to start your company?
Well, we’re four friends and we I mean, all four of us we really wanted to make our own board games.
So that was why you started then because you wanted to make your own board games?
Yes and we thought why not start a games company.
And so there are four of you?
That's right. Oh wait a minute, there's actually five members of the company.
We recently employed a new person, Sammy's dung.
If you're listening, hi Sammy!
So you're all from Hong Kong?
Yes, that’s right.
Hong Kong born and bred.
Well it’s nice to see a local company.
When did you form the company?
Two years ago in 2016.
OK, so quite a new company.
So Eric, Angel's company just started out.
They have an idea for a game.
They want to move ahead.
What advice would you give her and her company?
Well, supposing that you have developed a game, Yes, yes we have.
Right well, the next stage is obviously that you need to decide how to get funds to make your game.
Ah, of course.
Money. Yes, well, a small company needs to get funds to produce the game because producing the game can be quite expensive.
And I personally think that the best way to get funds is through Game Start.
Oh, OK. And what is Game Start?
Well, Game Start is the most well -known funding website for board game companies.
Right. So what's the main advantage of using Game Start as a source of funds then?
Well, I'd say the main advantage of something like Game Start is it’s global so Because it’s online.
Exactly, so you can get money from investors from, well basically, anywhere in the world.
OK, well, that sounds the way to go.
Yeah, Yeah, but don’t forget there are other ways besides Game Start to get funding.
Such as? Like, getting a grant from a local company.
OK. I mean, there are local grants available where you can win money as an award.
In Hong Kong, one of the best known of these is the Acorn Grant.
You might have heard of it.
Yeah, actually we’ve been looking into applying for the Acorn Grant.
Good, though with a grant like the ACON Grant there are definitely disadvantages.
Like what? Well often when you get a grant they tell you that they'll give you lots of help but really they just want to control everything.
The ACON Grant has the reputation for being one of those.
Really? Yeah, I’m afraid so.
Oh I don’t want that.
Me and my friends at Griffin Workshop just want to be independent.
We We don’t really want other people to control us.
Well, if you value your independence, then a grant like the ACON Grant maybe isn’t your best option.
OK, now Angel, back to the games that Griffin Workshop make.
Have you actually made any games yet?
Yeah, we've made two games.
We've published the first one and we are now working on the second one.
So tell us about the first one.
OK, our first game was called Death Kick.
Death Kick! Now that is a good name.
And it’s a card game.
A card game?
And from the sound of it, it’s a fighting game, I’m guessing.
Yeah. It’s a Kung Fu card game.
A Kung Fu card game!
Yeah, I've played Death Kick and I thought it was really good.
Oh wow! OK, well, tell us about your second game.
game. The latest one.
OK. Our latest game is called Escape to Hong Kong Island and is it a zombie game.
A zombie game, OK.
Is it set in Hong Kong?
Yes that’s right, set in Hong Kong.
OK, so what happens in the game?
Right well, the players start in Kowloon and OK, they’re in Kowloon.
Yes, and the players have to reach Hong Kong Island.
And so the first player who gets to Hong Kong Island is the winner.
Actually no. It’s a team game, so everybody in your team has to reach Hong Kong Island.
So if everybody in your team reaches Hong Kong Island, your team is the winner?
Is that the idea?
That's right. If all your team members manage to get to Hong Kong Island, that’s it you've won.
Sounds good. So Eric.
As an experienced game designer, designer.
what advice would you give Angel about Escape to Hong Kong Island?
Well, it sounds pretty interesting.
I would say that the first thing you need to do is be very clear who your target audience is.
Who’s your target audience for the game, Angel?
Young teenagers. OK.
Well, a word of warning then, young teenagers is often the trickiest age group to sell a game to.
And has your artist designed some of the artwork yet?
Yes. We have samples of artwork.
Well OK, one thing to always remember, if your audience is young teenagers, is that parents usually have the final say in whether the game gets bought or not.
Oh, OK. I mean, either parents themselves buy it for their kids for something like a birthday present or they’ll demand to see what their son or daughter has bought.
Oh. Very often you have to remind your artist about this.
Sometimes an artist will often get carried away and they'll produce this beautiful work, and that may well appeal to the young teenager, but the parents won’t approve because it’s just too graphic.
And by graphic you mean?
Too adult. Art that’s just too violent usually.
apparently. Parents won't buy or won't let their kids buy it.
Well, that’s some pretty sound advice for you there, Angel.
OK, I think we're out of time now and I'd like to thank you both for coming in to chat to us today.
